newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bond yields near lows, TCorp issuing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bond yields near lows, TCorp issuing.

text.p: *Australian bonds closed firm, although most of the trading action occurred in futures during the morning session amid the roll over to June from the now expired March contracts.
*TCorp to tender A$300 million of new 2008 benchmark bond.
Australian bond yields ended near the day's lows after rallying from Friday's overbought levels as fears of a possible tightening by the Federal Reserve eased slightly following the U.S. PPI report.
However, most of the local trading action occurred in futures during the morning session amid the roll over to June three and 10-year contracts from the now expired March bonds.

The 10-year bond yield had brushed 8.0 percent on Friday amid worries that the February PPI might show some inflation pressures, but in the event the index showed a weaker than expected 0.4 percent fall, its largest drop since October 1994.

The U.S. market is likely to stay jittery in the run up to Wednesday's February U.S. CPI and the debate over a potential tightening is expected trundle on all the way to the Federal Open Market Committee on March 25.
And in the absence of any major data this week, trading action locally is expected to be very much tied to events in the U.S., traders said.

However, Tuesday's morning session will feature a A$300 million tender by New South Wales Treasury Corp (TCorp) of a new 8.0 percent March 2008 benchmark stock. The result will be announced at around 10.20 a.m. (2320 GMT) on Tuesday.

TCorp said it will also look to issue up to an additional A$200 million of the 2008 bonds either through accepting oversubscriptions in the tender, or through consolidating out of the 2001, 2004, 2006 TCorp bonds into the new issue.

The launch of a new benchmark is consistent with TCorp's stated objective of maintaining a minimum of A$12.0 billion of domestic bonds outstanding, given the pending maturity of the 12.5 percent April 1997 bond, of which there is about A$1.0 billion on issue.

The local market's firm tone saw spreads to the U.S. and Canada narrow sharply, partially reversing Friday's severe underperformance. The yield curve continued last week's steepening trend with the local long end remaining wary of developments in the U.S.
The official cash settlement price for the expired March three-year contract was 93.13 and 92.150 for the 10-year.
